name: France
tagline: Public university costs €178 a year; the famous schools cost 100x that
summary: France splits sharply in two. Public universities are almost free — €178 a year for a licence in 2026/27, plus a €105 student-life contribution — and as an EU citizen you apply through Parcoursup, the national platform, in the winter before you start. The grandes écoles and private institutions are the other France: Sciences Po, École Polytechnique's bachelor, the business-school BBAs and the American University of Paris all run their own admissions, look at your whole profile, interview you, and charge between roughly €15,000 and €27,000 a year. Almost all the English-taught bachelor's degrees sit on that second side.
whyConsider: Public university tuition is €178 a year for a licence in 2026/27
Parcoursup is a genuine central system: one account, one timetable, up to 10 wishes that you do not have to rank
Sciences Po runs a dedicated route for foreign secondary diplomas with clear, dated rounds, and its fees are income-based down to €0 for EEA families
Serious English-taught bachelors exist at the grandes écoles: Sciences Po's English-track programmes, the École Polytechnique Bachelor of Science, ESCP's BSc in Management
France is a short train or flight from Denmark, so visiting before you commit is realistic
watchOuts: The English-taught options are overwhelmingly the expensive ones — the €178 public university largely teaches in French
Parcoursup runs on French-school logic and closes wishes in March, long before your IB results, so everything rides on predicted grades and your dossier

Grandes écoles fees are steep and mostly not income-adjusted: ESCP's BSc is €20,800 a year for European students in the 2027 intake, École Polytechnique's Bachelor €15,900, ESSEC's Global BBA €15,900 in year one and €18,900 after, and EDHEC's Global Business track €23,900
French universities can require proof of French (DELF/DALF or TCF) for French-taught degrees; requirements vary by institution, so check with the university

The Parcoursup 2027 calendar did not exist yet on 24 September 2026 - the official calendar page still showed the 2026 cycle, and the ministry publishes the next one in November or December, so treat the winter dates below as the shape of the year rather than as confirmed

ibRecognition.subjectLevelRule: Not defined nationally. Selective programmes read HL subjects as the equivalent of French specialities — Sciences Po states there are no specific subject requirements, while the École Polytechnique Bachelor expects a strong mathematics and science background.
ibRecognition.gradeConversion: No national IB-to-French conversion is published. On Parcoursup and at the grandes écoles your IB record is assessed qualitatively as part of the dossier, alongside school reports and, at Sciences Po, written essays and an interview.
notes: Sciences Po's international pathway is defined by the diploma you are sitting, not by your nationality: anyone taking a non-French secondary diploma, including the IB, uses it. Students sitting the French baccalauréat use Parcoursup instead.

Sciences Po scores the application out of 100: 50 points for the file (exam results, school record, essays and project statement) and 50 points for a remote interview covering a self-introduction, an image analysis and your motivations.
Sciences Po warns that AI-generated or plagiarised essays lead to disciplinary action, and that missing the interview means rejection.
EU, EEA and Swiss citizens apply for a first-year licence through Parcoursup, like French students; the DAP 'dossier vert' is for other nationalities (Ministry of Higher Education, 2026-2027 page).
No national minimum IB score exists; each programme sets its own bar.

deadlines.label: Parcoursup — registration and wishes open
deadlines.year: 2026 cycle — the 2027 opening date is not yet announced
deadlines.notes: The official Parcoursup calendar page (in French) published the 2026 cycle as "Du lundi 19 janvier au jeudi 12 mars 2026 : je m'inscris et je formule mes vœux". As of 24 September 2026 the page still shows only the 2026 calendar, so the 2027 opening date is not announced; the ministry normally publishes the next calendar in November or December. Context, not a milestone: the 2026 programme catalogue opened for browsing on 17 December 2025 ("Mercredi 17 décembre 2025 : je découvre la carte des formations Parcoursup 2026"), which is a browsing date rather than something you must do.

deadlines.label: École Polytechnique Bachelor — round 1 closes (2027 intake)
deadlines.notes: Published as "September 17, 2026 to October 20, 2026 at 11:59 PM (CEST)", with interviews in early December and results in January 2027. Rounds 2 and 3 follow, so missing this is not fatal. You may apply once a year, either here or through Parcoursup, not both. Application fee €105.

deadlines.label: École Polytechnique Bachelor — round 2 closes (2027 intake)
deadlines.notes: Published as "October 21, 2026 to January 6, 2027 at 11:59 PM (CET)"; interviews in February-March, results in March 2027.

deadlines.label: École Polytechnique Bachelor — final round closes (2027 intake)
deadlines.notes: Published as "January 7, 2027 to February 8, 2027 at 2 PM (CET)" - 2 pm, not midnight. Interviews in March-April, results in April 2027.

deadlines.label: EDHEC International BBA — first of five admission sessions closes (2027 intake)
deadlines.notes: EDHEC's international admissions page gives the first session as "from 1st October to 3rd November 2026", with an online English assessment and an online interview. Four later sessions run to March; applying in round 1 or 2 is what makes you eligible for its Excellence scholarships. Application fee €100.

deadlines.label: Sciences Po — first round for foreign secondary diplomas (2027 intake)
deadlines.notes: Sciences Po publishes all three round deadlines as "Paris time (11.59pm)". Apply by this date and you get your result in mid-January 2027 — the school publishes only the month, not a result day. The interview window for this round is a separate entry.

deadlines.label: Sciences Po — interviews, first round (2027 intake)
deadlines.notes: Published as "from 8 December 2026 until 18 December 2026". The remote interview is worth 50 of the 100 points, and Sciences Po states that missing it means rejection — so this window is a hard commitment, not a courtesy invitation. You are interviewed in this window if you applied in the 4 November 2026 round.

deadlines.label: Sciences Po — second round, and Émile Boutmy scholarship deadline (2027 intake)
deadlines.notes: Published as "Paris time (11.59pm)". Results at the beginning of April 2027 — the school publishes only the month. This is also the deadline to apply for the Émile Boutmy scholarship. The interview window for this round is a separate entry.

deadlines.label: Sciences Po — final round and dual-degree deadline (2027 intake)
deadlines.notes: Published as "Paris time (11.59pm)". Results in early May 2027 — the school publishes only the month. Dual degrees with Freie Universität Berlin, Hong Kong University, Keio, ESCP and Luiss also close on this date. The interview window for this round is a separate entry.

deadlines.label: Sciences Po — interviews, second round (2027 intake)
deadlines.notes: Published as "from 8 March 2027 until 19 March 2027". You are interviewed in this window if you applied in the 13 January 2027 round. Missing the interview means rejection.

deadlines.label: Sciences Po — interviews, final round (2027 intake)
deadlines.notes: Published as "from 13 April 2027 until 23 April 2027". You are interviewed in this window if you applied in the 1 March 2027 round. Missing the interview means rejection.

deadlines.label: Parcoursup — deadline to enter your wishes
deadlines.year: 2027 entry — the 2027 calendar is not yet published
deadlines.notes: On 24 September 2026 the official Parcoursup calendar page still showed only the 2026 calendar, whose wording was "Jeudi 12 mars 2026 : dernier jour pour formuler mes vœux". No 2027 date exists yet; the ministry normally publishes the following year's calendar in November or December, so expect the 2027 date around mid-March 2027 and re-check the same page from December 2026. Aggregator sites already print 13 March 2027, but they label it prévisionnel and it is not on any official page, so it is not recorded here.

deadlines.label: Parcoursup — deadline to confirm your wishes
deadlines.year: 2027 entry — the 2027 calendar is not yet published
deadlines.notes: On 24 September 2026 the official Parcoursup calendar page still showed only the 2026 calendar, whose wording was "Mercredi 1er avril 2026 : dernier jour pour compléter mon dossier et confirmer mes vœux". A wish you do not confirm is lost, so this is the second hard gate and it falls about three weeks after the first. No 2027 date is published yet.

deadlines.label: Parcoursup — admission phase: answering the offers you receive
deadlines.year: 2027 entry — the 2027 calendar is not yet published
deadlines.notes: Once the admission phase opens you must answer each offer within a short published window or lose it, so this is a period you have to be reachable in, not a single date. The 2026 calendar ran it as "Mardi 2 juin 2026 : début de la phase d'admission" through "Samedi 11 juillet 2026 : fin de la phase principale", with the complementary phase from 11 June 2026 to 10 September 2026 and response deadlines suspended during the baccalauréat written exams. The 2027 equivalents were not yet published on 24 September 2026.

deadlines.label: CVEC payment before administrative enrolment
deadlines.notes: There is no fixed national date: the CVEC portal, read in French on 2026-09-23, says to pay "au plus près de votre inscription effective" and that payment must be made "préalablement à son inscription", because the attestation is what lets you enrol. In practice that means from early July once you have definitively accepted a place. Context, not a milestone: the same page gives 31 May 2027 as the close of the 2026-2027 refund campaign, which only concerns students who paid and were in fact exempt.

steps: Decide which France you are applying to: public university via Parcoursup, or a grande école / private institution on its own timetable.

For a public university, create your Parcoursup account when the platform opens in January and enter your wishes before the March deadline — pre-registration on Parcoursup is compulsory for European students entering the first year of a licence.
Confirm each wish and complete your dossier by the early-April deadline, uploading transcripts, predicted IB grades and a motivation section for each wish.

For Sciences Po, École Polytechnique, ESSEC, ESCP, EDHEC or AUP, apply directly on the school's own platform in its own round — Sciences Po's 2027 rounds close on 4 November 2026, 13 January 2027 and 1 March 2027.
Sit any interview the school requires; Sciences Po's is remote and worth half your score.
Accept an offer, pay the €105 CVEC online, then complete administrative enrolment with the institution and pay the tuition.
Apply for CAF housing assistance and set up French health cover once you arrive.
application.selectionNotes: Public university licences split into non-selective (you are ranked but capacity-constrained) and selective (IUT, BTS, CPGE, art and design), all inside Parcoursup. The grandes écoles sit outside Parcoursup for foreign-diploma holders and select on dossier plus interview, sometimes plus a written test.

language.englishTaughtBachelors: Concentrated almost entirely in the grandes écoles and private institutions — Sciences Po's English-track programmes, the École Polytechnique Bachelor of Science, ESCP's BSc in Management, the BBAs at ESSEC, EDHEC and emlyon, and the American University of Paris. No official national count is published.
language.englishProof: Set institution by institution. ESCP asks for IELTS 6.5 or equivalent for its BSc in Management. Sciences Po expects high English proficiency and sets language requirements per programme. Whether IB English A or B is accepted in place of a test is not confirmed here; check with each institution.
notes: French is not required for the English-taught grande école programmes, but Sciences Po's bachelor is multilingual and some ESCP courses at the Paris campus are taught in French in years 2 and 3.
For a French-taught public university degree you will normally need to prove French, typically through DELF/DALF or TCF. The exact level varies by institution; check with the university.
Everyday life, part-time work and administration all run in French regardless of your degree.

tuitionEuEea.value: Public universities: €178 a year for a licence (reduced rate €118), €255 for a master's, €398 for a doctorate, and €2,620 for an engineering diploma. On top of that every student pays the CVEC of €105. Grandes écoles are separate: Sciences Po undergraduate is €0–€14,900 depending on household income for EEA fiscal residents; École Polytechnique's Bachelor of Science is €15,900; ESCP's BSc in Management is €20,800 for the 2027 intake.

tuitionNonEu.value: Public universities charge differentiated fees to non-EU/EEA students: €2,902 a year for a licence and €3,950 for a master's in 2026/27, set by decree no. 2026-385 of 19 May 2026; universities may exempt up to 30% of them. Grandes écoles: Sciences Po charges a flat €14,900 to students with fiscal residence outside the EEA; École Polytechnique's Bachelor is €19,200; ESCP's BSc is €26,800 for the 2027 intake.

costs.applicationFee: Sciences Po charges €150, non-refundable and waived only for refugees. École Polytechnique's Bachelor charges €105, EDHEC's BBA €100 and ESCP's BSc €80. Parcoursup itself is free.

livingCostMonthly.value: About €600-800 a month for housing, food and transport, according to Campus France; Paris costs noticeably more.

notes: The CVEC (Contribution de vie étudiante et de campus) is €105 for 2026/27, is paid online at cvec.etudiant.gouv.fr, and you cannot complete enrolment without the attestation. Scholarship holders and refugees are exempt but still need an exemption attestation.

Sciences Po's fee depends on the tax household's resources, not on nationality: an EEA family below roughly €42,000 combined income pays nothing, and the ceiling applies only at very high incomes. Figures beyond the €0–€14,900 range are not confirmed here.
Some non-EU students pay the EU rate anyway — residents of Quebec, holders of long-term residence cards and doctoral candidates among them.
If you transfer your enrolment between two institutions, €23 is retained by the first one.
The living-cost figure is Campus France's general guide, not an official survey; rents vary more than anything else, and Paris is the outlier.

funding.note: The programme must be SU-approved, and outside the Nordics SU is capped at four years (48 klip).

funding: CAF housing benefit (APL/ALS) is open to students in France including EU citizens, and meaningfully reduces rent; apply after you have a lease.
Sciences Po's Émile Boutmy scholarship for undergraduate applicants, with a 13 January 2027 deadline for the 2027 intake.
CROUS bourses sur critères sociaux, which also exempt you from the CVEC and from tuition; eligibility for EU nationals depends on residence conditions not confirmed here; check with CROUS.
Grandes écoles and business schools run their own merit scholarships, usually assessed at application.
Erasmus+ for an exchange period inside the degree.
workRights: EU/EEA citizens have full labour-market access in France with no permit and no hour cap. Non-EU students on a student residence permit may work up to 964 hours a year (60% of the legal annual working time) without a separate work authorisation (service-public.gouv.fr).
residency: As an EU/EEA citizen you need no visa and no residence permit. Travel on your passport or national ID card. There is no compulsory EU registration in France, but you will need a French bank account (for CAF and rent), a French phone number and a social-security number, so start those in your first weeks. Non-EU students apply for a VLS-TS student visa through the Études en France procedure before departure.
housing: CROUS student residences are cheap but scarce and allocated mainly on social criteria. Most students rent studios or shared flats privately, and French landlords normally demand a French guarantor — the state Visale scheme exists to replace one, and is worth arranging early. Paris is very expensive and very competitive; Lille, Strasbourg, Grenoble, Lyon and Nice are far easier. Start in May or June for a September start.
healthcare: Bring a European Health Insurance Card. Students staying for a full degree register with the French health system through etudiant-etranger.ameli.fr to obtain a social-security number and a carte Vitale, then usually add a mutuelle (top-up insurance) because the state reimburses only part of most costs.

institutions.name: Sciences Po
institutions.city: Paris, plus campuses in Dijon, Le Havre, Menton, Nancy, Poitiers and Reims
institutions.englishBachelors: Several English-track undergraduate programmes across the regional campuses
institutions.note: The obvious target for an IB student who wants social sciences in English, with a published route for foreign diplomas, a remote interview worth half the score, and income-based fees down to zero.

institutions.name: École Polytechnique
institutions.englishBachelors: Bachelor of Science, taught entirely in English, with double majors in Mathematics & Physics, Mathematics & Computer Science, or Mathematics & Economics
institutions.note: France's most famous engineering school; its three-year English-taught Bachelor is small, extremely mathematical, and about 80% international.

institutions.name: ESCP Business School
institutions.city: Paris, with campuses in Berlin, London, Madrid and Turin
institutions.englishBachelors: BSc in Management, taught mainly in English across three campuses in three countries
institutions.note: You spend the three years on three different European campuses; €20,800 a year for European students in the 2027 intake, €26,800 for non-Europeans, plus an €80 application fee.

institutions.name: ESSEC Business School
institutions.englishBachelors: Global BBA, four years, with an English track on the Cergy campus (and in Singapore and Rabat).
institutions.note: One of France's top three business schools; its four-year Global BBA costs €15,900 in year one and €18,900 a year after that (2026/27 intake), plus a €5,500 deposit on admission. 2027 deadlines were not on the page.

institutions.name: EDHEC Business School
institutions.englishBachelors: International BBA, with the Global Business track taught in English.
institutions.note: Strong in finance, with campuses in Lille and Nice. The BBA's Global Business track costs €23,900 a year and the Business Management track €15,900; the first of five sessions for the 2027 intake closes on 3 November 2026.

institutions.name: emlyon business school
institutions.englishBachelors: Global BBA, four years, with French and English tracks.
institutions.note: Lyon is a far cheaper city than Paris, and emlyon's BBA lets you spend up to 75% of it abroad; first-year fees for the 2027 intake are €15,500 a year.

institutions.name: The American University of Paris
institutions.englishBachelors: The entire undergraduate curriculum is taught in English, on a US liberal-arts model
institutions.note: A small English-language liberal-arts college in central Paris that runs dedicated IB Diploma scholarships; tuition figures are not confirmed here; check with the college.

institutions.name: Sorbonne Université
institutions.englishBachelors: Very limited at bachelor level; most licence teaching is in French
institutions.note: Formed in 2018 from Paris-Sorbonne and Pierre-et-Marie-Curie; the classic €178-a-year French public university, if your French is up to it.

institutions.name: Université Paris-Saclay
institutions.englishBachelors: Limited at bachelor level; an international bachelor track exists in the sciences
institutions.note: France's highest-ranked research university, especially in mathematics and physics, on a large science campus south of Paris.

institutions.name: Université PSL
institutions.englishBachelors: One undergraduate programme taught entirely in English, the International Bachelor of Science in AI; Sustainability Sciences moves from 40% English in year one to 100% in year three.
institutions.note: A collegiate university grouping ENS, Dauphine, Mines Paris and others, with a small and highly selective undergraduate programme.

institutions.name: Université Grenoble Alpes
institutions.englishBachelors: Some English-taught bachelor tracks, including an international bachelor programme
institutions.note: A strong science university in the Alps, with lower rents than Paris and skiing an hour away. UGA's main site is in French; its English pages for prospective international students are at international.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr, which is where the admissions link points.

institutions.name: Université de Strasbourg
institutions.englishBachelors: Limited at bachelor level; some English-taught European and international tracks
institutions.note: A major research university on the German border, in a bilingual city that is also home to the European Parliament. Unistra's main site is in French; its English guidance for applicants from abroad is at international-welcome.unistra.fr, which is where the admissions link points.
